newsitem.title: UK: FORECAST - Growth to lift Australian stocks.
newsitem.headline: FORECAST - Growth to lift Australian stocks.

text.p: Continuing economic growth, particularly in the resource sector benefiting from higher commodity prices, should buoy Australian equities in 1997, according to economists polled by Reuters.

Twelve equity analysts predicted on average that the Australian All Ordinaries Index would reach around 2,570 by the end of this year, representing a rise of about five percent from the 2,454.4 close on March 12.
The survey, conducted last week, showed an expectation that Australian stocks would rise 11 percent to 2,720 by the end of 1998, according to an average from eight analysts.

These forecasts are little changed from those made in a Reuters equities survey at the end of 1996, although predictions for 1998 were pared back slightly because of fears that interest rates may rise or the expected lift in resources may fail to materialise.
GREG MATTHEWS, EXECUTIVE DIRECTOR AUSTRALIAN EQUITIES, MERCANTILE MUTUAL INVESTMENT MANAGEMENT:
"It's still a pretty favourable environment for equities with some profit growth and inflation staying low and bond rates behaving themselves."
PETER MUNCKTON, SENIOR ECONOMIST, BANKERS TRUST AUSTRALIA.
"As you go through the course of 1998, there may be concerns about rising interest rates, and that might choke off too much more appreciation, particularly in the second half of the year."
